title: Pricing experiments analysis – working notes (messy)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-23 (Chris)

Purpose
- Scratchpad for pricing/packaging experiment analysis across Hosted API + Dedicated adjacencies.
- This doc is intentionally messy. The cleaned version should land in Confluence readout + enablement materials.

Where things live (links / pointers)
- Experiment registry (source of truth for variants/eligibility): Confluence → pricing-experiment-catalog-2025h2-2026q1
- Readout draft: Confluence → pricing-experiment-analysis-readout-2026q1 (DON’T copy numbers from here until we lock exclusions)
- Meter definitions + edge cases: Confluence → hosted-api-meter-definitions-v3
- Invoice mapping: Confluence → invoice-line-item-mapping-to-telemetry
- Rounding + streaming accounting decision: Confluence → adr-027-meter-rounding-and-streaming-accounting

Dashboards / queries (placeholders; update with actual links)
- Looker: “Pricing Experiments – Funnel + Retention (Self-serve)” → https://looker.redwoodinference.internal/dashboards/px_funnel_retention
- Looker: “Token Economics – GM bridge (by model/region/tier)” → https://looker.redwoodinference.internal/dashboards/unit_econ_gm_bridge
- Metabase: “Experiment assignments QA (eligibility + bucketing)” → https://metabase.redwoodinference.internal/question/1182
- BigQuery saved query folder: bq://redwood-analytics/pricing_experiments/q1_2026/
- Console vs invoice alignment tracker (QA): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/CONSOLE_INVOICE_ALIGNMENT_QA (TODO: replace)


Experiments in scope (Q1 cycle)
NOTE: names are not consistent across tools; see registry for canonical exp_id.

1) EXP-HOSTED-001 “Free credits restructure”
- Hypothesis: lower upfront credits reduces abuse + improves early margin without hurting activation
- Variants (approx):
  - Control: $X credits on signup (one-time)
  - Variant A: smaller signup credits + milestone credits after first successful invoice
  - Variant B: smaller signup credits + requires phone verification to unlock full credits
- Primary metrics:
  - Activation: 7d first_successful_call, 7d token usage > threshold
  - Conversion: paid conversion by day 30/45
  - Fraud/abuse proxy: multi-account clusters, chargebacks, unusual request patterns
- Guardrails:
  - Support tickets (billing/pricing confusion)
  - Paid churn < baseline

2) EXP-HOSTED-004 “Overage tiering / price-per-token”
- Hypothesis: tiered overage reduces sticker shock + improves expansion while keeping GM stable
- Variants:
  - Control: flat overage rate
  - Variant: step-down overage rate past monthly token threshold
- Needs careful GM bridge (cache hit rates differ by cohorts)

3) EXP-HOSTED-006 “Plan gating: access to premium model families”
- Hypothesis: gating drives conversion for teams needing top models; minimal churn impact for long-tail
- Variants:
  - Control: broad catalog on paid plans
  - Variant: restrict certain model families behind Pro/Enterprise
- Risks:
  - Customers switching endpoints/regions to bypass gating (watch for sudden model alias changes)
  - Increased support/CS escalations

4) EXP-DEDICATED-002 “Commit structure (burn-down + burst)”
- Hypothesis: a simpler commit + defined burst rate improves close rate and expansion
- This isn’t purely self-serve, so measurement is messy (sales-assisted, negotiation).
- Metrics:
  - Close rate / time to close
  - Expansion within 90d
  - Gross margin vs expected
  - Commit burn-down comprehension (support load)


Cohort definitions (WIP)
We need to be explicit because multiple teams are pulling different cuts.

A) Population
- Hosted self-serve cohort (primary):
  - First_seen_at between 2025-12-01 and 2026-02-15
  - acquired via self-serve signup (exclude sales-assisted accounts; heuristic below)
  - include: customers with any hosted_api request
  - exclude: sandbox/internal/test orgs
- Sales-assisted / enterprise cohort (secondary):
  - has Salesforce opportunity OR HubSpot lifecycle stage >= “SQL” OR contract_type in {Dedicated, Private}
  - Note: classification differs by CRM hygiene; Isabelle to confirm rules

B) “Activated” definition (for funnel analysis)
- Activated_7d = within 7 days of signup:
  - >= 1 successful request_outcome = success
  - AND total_output_tokens + total_input_tokens >= 10,000 (tunable)
- Alternative: “meaningful” activation requires streaming usage OR tool calling usage? (open)

C) Paid conversion
- Paid_45d = has invoice_run with amount_due > $0 within 45 days OR plan_status = paid AND spend > $0
- Note: credits complicate “amount_due > 0” (watch invoices fully offset by credits)

D) Retention
- Retained_m1 = any billable tokens in days 31–60 after signup
- Retained_m2 = any billable tokens in days 61–90
- For enterprises: use monthly active usage, but commit structures distort “billable” (need separate definition)

E) Expansion
- Expansion_90d = 90d trailing spend growth > 20% vs first paid month (or absolute increase threshold)
- For Dedicated: expansion may show as contract amendment not immediate usage spike

F) Segments we must cut by (minimum)
- customer_tier: self_serve | growth | enterprise (proxy by ARR/spend bands)
- model_family: llama | mistral | qwen | “other” (use Redwood alias mapping)
- region: us-east | us-west | eu-central | ap-southeast
- workload_type proxy:
  - chat_completions vs embeddings vs rerank
  - streaming_used = true/false
  - avg_prompt_tokens band


Bucketing / assignment checks
- Confirm deterministic bucketing key:
  - Is it org_id or billing_account_id? (I think org_id today; check instrumentation)
  - What happens when org merges / billing entity changes mid-cycle?
- “Eligibility” gotcha:
  - If eligibility depends on plan, and plan depends on experiment outcome, we can get post-treatment bias
  - Need to define “eligible at exposure time”
- QA queries to run:
  - assignment_ratio by day (should be stable)
  - assignment_ratio by region/model_family (should be random; if not, we broke bucketing)


Data sources (current)
- Telemetry events (raw): metering_events_* (Logan/Nadia)
- Billing-ready aggregates: billing_usage_daily + billing_usage_invoice_window (Emily)
- Experiment assignment: experiment_assignments (Product analytics)
- CRM: HubSpot/Salesforce exports (Isabelle)
- Support signals: Jira tags for billing/pricing tickets + Slack escalations (Dev Patel)

Important: reconcile the “usage” used for experiment analysis with the “usage” that drives invoices. Don’t present results that will later be undermined by meter fixes.


Known measurement caveats / exclusions (VERY IMPORTANT)
These should likely be consistent across all experiments.

1) Streaming disconnect accounting bug (confirmed)
- Impact: some sessions billed tokens after client disconnect (overstated output tokens)
- Fix: github:redwood/pr_41903 + linear:ENG-4822
- Exclusion / handling proposal:
  - Exclude affected window until backfill lands OR flag as “pre-fix” and run sensitivity
  - We need exact dates when fix rolled out + backfill window (Ethan/Nadia)

2) Rounding mismatch (console vs invoice)
- ADR says per-request rounding removed; invoice aggregator now aligns to per-invoice aggregation
- Fix: github:redwood/pr_41888
- For experiment analysis:
  - Use billing-ready aggregates post-fix if possible
  - If mixing windows, compute tokens at highest granularity and aggregate ourselves (Mei)

3) Retry/double-counting risk (suspected; one endpoint)
- Slack mention: retries being double-counted for one endpoint (thread: slack:eng/1707853312)
- If request_outcome dimension wasn’t present historically, we may be counting tokens from failed + retried requests
- Fix: github:redwood/pr_41917 + linear:ENG-4823 (adds request_outcome/retry dimensions)
- Exclusion proposal:
  - Exclude endpoints where retries are high and instrumentation incomplete
  - Or exclude requests with ambiguous outcome (but that may drop too much)

4) Internal/test accounts
- Must exclude:
  - Redwood employees
  - load-test orgs
  - partner test tenants
- Need canonical list / query (Mei: please pin a reference table)

5) Credits / invoice “amount_due” pitfalls
- If we use “paid” = invoice amount_due > 0, then credits can hide conversion
- Better: paid_plan_status OR payment_method_on_file? (open)

6) Backfills and time windows
- Backfills will create spikes/deltas; SRE wants alert suppression rules during backfills
- For analysis, avoid windows where billing aggregates were regenerated unless we re-pull after backfill completes


Primary analyses (notes + to-dos)

A) Funnel: signup → activation → conversion
- Need consistent “first exposure” timestamp
  - Is exposure when user visits pricing page? when they first call API? when they see credit offer?
  - Today we mostly have assignment at signup, so treat signup as exposure
- For free credits restructure:
  - Watch for “activation” inflation from abuse accounts. Consider fraud filters BEFORE computing activation rates.

B) Retention / churn risk signals
- For plan gating experiment:
  - We should track:
    - downgrade events
    - model_family switches (if gated model usage disappears, do they churn or swap?)
    - support tickets about “suddenly blocked”

C) Unit economics / GM
- GM impact needs:
  - revenue per token (varies by plan + experiment)
  - cost per token (varies by model family + region + cache hit rate)
- Rishi note: be careful with mix shift; expansions often move to cheaper models and increase batching efficiency
- TODO: define GM_calc_v1 consistent with FP&A sheet assumptions

D) Statistical approach (Sana notes)
- Default: difference in proportions for conversion; log-rank / survival for time-to-convert; Mann-Whitney for spend distribution?
- Minimum reporting:
  - sample sizes, confidence intervals
  - multiple testing adjustment (we have too many cuts)
  - pre-registered primary metrics vs exploratory cuts
- Concern: cohort bias (self-serve seasonality, holiday effects) → use time fixed effects / stratification by signup week


Open questions (need answers before readout)
1) Eligibility + bucketing
- Are we bucketing by org_id across all experiments or by experiment-specific logic?
- Are “growth” accounts (sales touched but not enterprise) included in self-serve dashboards?

2) Definition of “conversion” for credits-heavy plans
- Should conversion be: “adds payment method” vs “first invoice sent” vs “first invoice paid”?
- Finance preference: invoice issued? But Product wants earlier signal.

3) Dedicated attribution
- For EXP-DEDICATED-002, do we attribute usage to commit burn-down or on-demand overage first?
- How does burst capacity get reported (invoice line item vs included)?
- We need a one-pager from Finance/RevOps: how to interpret burn-down vs invoice for customer comms

4) Model alias mapping
- Chloe flagged that console usage uses model aliases that don’t match invoice mapping in some cases (fixed in github:redwood/pr_41941?)
- If analysis uses telemetry model_name and sales uses console display name, we will get confusion

5) Treatment of cached tokens
- Are cached tokens billed differently in any experiment variants? (I think no, but check)
- For unit economics: cost is much lower, revenue is same → mix shift can dominate results

6) Customer-level clustering
- For conversion/retention stats, do we analyze at org-level or user-level?
- Need to ensure one org doesn’t count multiple times due to multiple workspaces


Notes from meetings / random scraps
- 2026-02-05: Product/Finance sync: Laura wants “audit-ready” numbers before we announce any pricing win. She specifically asked for “how many invoices might change due to meter fixes” separate from “experiment impact”.
- 2026-02-08: Sana: please stop slicing by 12 dimensions simultaneously in readout slides; pick 2–3 pre-registered segments + label others exploratory.
- 2026-02-11: Isabelle: AEs are quoting during experiment; need a clear rule on whether discounts stack with credits (pending enablement deck).
- 2026-02-14: Mei: early query shows Variant A increased paid conversion but also increased average tokens/user; could be mix shift to embeddings? Need breakdown by endpoint.


To-do list (owner / due)
- [Mei] Provide canonical cohort tables (self-serve vs sales-assisted) with exclusion list joined in (due 2026-02-26)
- [Sana] Proposed statistical template + what we can claim / cannot claim (due 2026-02-27)
- [Emily] Confirm exact billing aggregate versions and backfill windows relevant to Q1 analysis (due 2026-02-28)
- [Chloe] Confirm model alias mapping parity console vs invoice for analysis dimensions (due 2026-02-28)
- [Chris] Draft readout narrative with explicit caveats + decision asks (due 2026-03-01)


Appendix: quick “do not do this” list for the readout
- Do not compare console usage totals to invoice totals without stating rounding + timezone handling.
- Do not claim GM improvements without stating model/region mix shift and cache hit changes.
- Do not publish conversion numbers without clarifying credits treatment (amount_due vs paid_plan).
- Do not ignore streaming bug window; customers are already sensitive and Support has active tickets.
